Diesel prices hit several new records, surging to over $6 per gallon in September. They are rising faster than gasoline prices, and that matters disproportionately because diesel is a core input for freight, heavy industry, agriculture and construction.
   Higher diesel prices can show up in inflation through business costs first, then potentially affect consumer prices over time depending on pass-through and demand.
